changes.reason: [civil-code 138 ¶1] makes the custodian with power of use, management and control liable for the thing's harm; [civil-code 138 ¶2] is kept as its own statement, the custodian's release on proof of an unforeseen cause.
[civil-code 131 ¶1] has the judge assess compensation under articles 182 and 182 مكرر and lets him reserve the victim's right to a new assessment.
[civil-code 182 ¶1] gives the elements (loss suffered and gain missed), to which [civil-code 131 ¶1] refers; ¶2 concerns contractual obligations only and is not cited.

changes.reason: [civil-code 132 ¶2] makes compensation a sum of money and allows restoration of the former state only at the victim's request and at the judge's discretion, so the request asks for the sum and, in the alternative, restoration.

changes.catalogueSays: احتياطيا: تعيين خبير لمعاينة الأضرار وتقديرها
changes.reason: [cpca 126 ¶1] lets the judge appoint an expert at a party's request, and [cpca 125 ¶1] sets the expert's role on a technical fact.
[cpca 310 ¶2] and [cpca 77 ¶1] allow a finding of the state of things before the claim; it is evidence and no text makes it a condition of admissibility.
Evidence of the harm that [civil-code 138 ¶1] and [civil-code 182 ¶1] require; no text governs it.
[cpca 125 ¶1] defines the expert's role; a report already in hand supports the assessment under [civil-code 182 ¶1].

Custody is defined by power of use, management and control in [civil-code 138 ¶1]; for an animal the keeper answers even if not the owner [civil-code 139 ¶1]; for a building collapse the text names the owner, not the custodian [civil-code 140 ¶2].
The harm and its extent are assessed under [civil-code 131 ¶1] and [civil-code 182 ¶1]; its date starts the period of [civil-code 133 ¶1], imported from the periods module.
[civil-code 139 ¶1] is the special text for harm by an animal, which the catalogue folds into article 138.
[civil-code 140 ¶2] is the special text for a building's collapse, with the owner as defendant and its own grounds of release.
The defendant bears the proof of the ground of release: [civil-code 138 ¶2], [civil-code 139 ¶1], [civil-code 140 ¶2].
[civil-code 182 مكرر ¶1] covers moral harm, to which [civil-code 131 ¶1] refers.
[civil-code 132 ¶1] and [civil-code 132 ¶2] set the manner of compensation (instalments, annuity, money, restoration).
[civil-code 177 ¶1] allows reduction for the victim's contributory fault; its reach to this claim is a reading (open point o4).
[civil-code 126 ¶1] makes several persons responsible for a harmful act jointly liable; its reach to custodians is a reading.
[civil-code 323 ¶1] on the burden of proof and [civil-code 333 ¶1] on witness proof of legal acts, both applied by reading to the material facts of this claim.
[cpca 419 ¶1] puts the costs on the losing party.
[cpca 323 ¶3] lets the judge order provisional execution in case of urgency.
[civil-code 131 ¶1] allows reserving the victim's right to a new assessment within a set time.
Liability rests on custody [civil-code 138 ¶1] or keeping [civil-code 139 ¶1] or ownership of the building [civil-code 140 ¶2], so the defendant's link with the thing must be proved.
Bodily harm and repair costs are part of the loss assessed under [civil-code 182 ¶1].
The record's own section rule proposes the civil section on the imported statements of [cpca 32 ¶3], [cpca 32 ¶4] and [cpca 32 ¶5]; the choice is a reading.
[civil-code 140 ¶1] makes the holder liable for a fire's harm only on proof of fault, a different regime; a proposed slot asks whether the harm came from a fire.
[civil-code 554 ¶1] and [civil-code 557 ¶1] give a ten-year guarantee against architect and contractor, with its own three-year limitation.
[civil-code 140 مكرر ¶1] makes the producer liable for a defective product.
[civil-code 124 ¶1] rests liability for one's own act on fault.
[civil-code 134 ¶1] and [civil-code 136 ¶1] govern liability for persons under supervision and for agents.
[civil-code 140 ¶3] gives the threatened person a claim for preventive measures before any collapse.
[civil-code 140 مكرر 1 ¶1] puts on the State the compensation of bodily harm when no one is liable.
[civil-code 138 ¶1] is the general rule; the special road-accident regime is not in the store (requested; open point o2).
Tort claims go to the court of the place of the harmful act under [cpca 39 ¶3], with the general rule of [cpca 37 ¶1].

A public administrative custodian sends the case to the administrative courts except for vehicle damage, and an offence on the same facts raises the criminal route; the module carries the texts, among them [cpca 39 ¶3] and [civil-code 339 ¶1].
The compensation action falls after the period of [civil-code 133 ¶1] from the day of the harmful act; the module holds its counting and readings.
No notice is needed when the obligation is compensation for a harmful act [civil-code 181 ¶3]; the module's step carries the exemption.
The petition's particulars, standing, interest, capacity, fees and language apply to every petition; the module rests on [cpca 15 ¶1] among others.
The only period found for this claim is that of [civil-code 133 ¶1], imported; no forfeiture specific to this claim was found in the unit's texts.
No step before filing is required by the texts; the notice step is imported only to show its exemption under [civil-code 181 ¶3].
